problem: Consider the function $f(x)={x}^{2}+{2}^{x}$ and the point $P(0,1)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(1,0)$ is$\,${{field-1}}.

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function
examples.problem: Consider the function $f(x) = \dfrac{2-3x}{4+5x}$ and the point $P\left(-1,-5\right)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y=f^{-1}(x)$ at the point $\left(-5,-1\right).$
examples.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(-1, -5).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{2-3x}{4+5x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{22}{(4+5x)^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =-22\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(-1, -5)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(-5, -1)$ lies on $y=f^{-1}(x).$ 

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(-5) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(-5))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-22)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{22}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

The figure above shows the graph of a function $y=f(x)$ and its inverse $y={f}^{-1}(x).$ The point $A$ has coordinates $(-1,2)$ and lies on $y=f(x).$ The point $B$ has coordinates $(2,-1)$ and lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$ If ${f}^{′}(-1)=-2,$ what is $({f}^{-1})^{′}(2)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $B\,(2,-1)$ lies on ${f}^{-1},$ we have ${f}^{-1}(2)=-1.$
We're also told that ${f}^{′}(-1)=-2.$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse function is

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Evaluating at $x=2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(2) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(2))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-2)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
